history.sg_progress: The Administration conducts annual monitoring of progress across the Secretariat. In 2024, a communication was issued to all entities to highlight the status of geographical representation and to reinforce the need to accelerate efforts to improve the representation of unrepresented and underrepresented Member States. The message emphasized the importance of addressing imbalances in geographical distribution, reiterated the expectations of the General Assembly and drew attention to retirement forecasts, which present a strategic opportunity to advance progress towards distribution targets. In addition, the Office of Human Resources is collaborating actively with entities on targeted outreach initiatives and providing guidance to support the sourcing of diverse talent from unrepresented and underrepresented Member States. In August 2025, the Assistant Secretary-General for Human Resources reached out to entities to seek their continued support in promoting equitable geographical distribution, while also encouraging efforts to strengthen internal capacity. Owing to the liquidity crisis, the Secretariat had to introduce cash conservation measures, which undermined the ability of entities to fill vacant positions. Unless the liquidity situation improves, the Administration’s efforts to improve equitable geographical distribution through recruitment will be hampered.

history.recommendation_text: The Board also recommends that the Administration take proactive measures targeting those entities that do not fulfil the established targets in order to improve the representation of those underrepresented and unrepresented countries.
history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. The Office of Human Resources has taken proactive measures to directly engage those entities that do not meet established targets. In this regard, the Assistant Secretary-General for Human Resources formally communicated with all heads of entities (email dated 14 August 2025) to highlight entity-level accountability for selection decisions, draw attention to gaps in representation from unrepresented and underrepresented Member States and encourage corrective action. This engagement is complemented by targeted outreach and the implementation of initiatives such as talent pipeline programmes to support entities with persistent challenges in improving geographical representation.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Office of Human Resources has taken proactive measures to directly engage those entities that do not meet established targets and formally communicated with all heads of entities (email dated 14 August 2025) to highlight entity-level accountability for selection decisions, draw attention to gaps in representation from unrepresented and underrepresented Member States and encourage corrective action, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
